title: Spread Life: Ginger — its history and lore, the health evidence, and the plant itself
question: What is known about ginger (Zingiber officinale) across its documented history and lore, the human health evidence, and the plant's own biology, and where do those three records support, complicate or contradict each other?
authors: Actualizer (commissioned review, drafted with Claude; Daniel Adamek, editor)
plain_abstract: Ginger read three ways at once: what dated historical documents say people did with it, what human trials show it does, and what is known about the plant and its chemistry. Written as a reference for the UAH Greenhouse team, with 32 historical recipes linked to the science. It reports where the evidence is good, where it is thin, and where nobody has looked.
audience: the UAH Greenhouse team and interested students

permissions.text: builder-authored; quotations from copyrighted sources are 25 words or fewer, in quotation marks and attributed; public-domain historical texts (published 1929 or earlier) are reproduced in the recipes section from scanned editions, each cited
permissions.figures: synthesised by the builder from cited data; no published figure images reproduced

verification_level: Of 162 references, 23 were read in full (historical sources from scanned public-domain editions, and the 2025 EU monograph), 121 from abstracts and 18 from record pages, fragments or a secondary tabulation. Each reference carries its read level; stated on /methods.
